## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sāḷiyajātaka* (Ja 367) is a narrative belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon, titled *The Hedgehog* in English translation [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework recorded in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, the Buddha delivered the discourse while residing at the Bamboo Grove (Veḷuvana), prompted by the remark that Devadatta could not even cause fear or alarm (*āvuso Devadatto tāsakārako pi bhavituṁ nâsakkhi*) [Fausböll 1883; SuttaCentral]. The story of the past is set in Bārāṇasī during the reign of King Brahmadatta, where the Bodhisatta was born into the family of a landowner (*kuṭumbiyakula*), opening with the verse beginning *Yo 'yaṁ sāliyachapo* [Fausböll 1883]. The title also appears listed in the *Dhammapada* commentary tradition [Burlingame 1921].

The verse material of the *Sāḷiyajātaka* shares widely attested gnomic and doctrinal parallels across early Buddhist literature. SuttaCentral identifies passage-level parallels in the Pali canon with the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 125), the *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 1.22 and SN 7.4), and the *Sutta Nipāta* (Snp 3.10), as well as the *Patna Dharmapada* (Kalyāṇīvagga, verses 96–120) [SuttaCentral]. Beyond Pali, the verse parallels the *Pāpavarga* of the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 28), its Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 28), and Chinese translations including T 210, T 212, and T 213 [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse computations by DharmaNexus confirm this transmission, showing Pali-internal alignment (§1.2–5.4) with the third volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* and cross-language alignment between the verse (§4.1) and the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (D0326), directly corroborating SuttaCentral's curated parallels [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral].
